title: The Four Salvations: how the soul is delivered in successive stages
reading:
The Lord's saving of the soul does not happen all at once. It unfolds in successive stages, each at a different register of his going-forth, and each stage delivers what could not yet be received at the previous one. Where one stage reaches its limit, the next is sent.

The first deliverance comes when the Divine Human goes forth into the soul's contest. At the moment the natural mind has organized itself under self-love and seems entirely held by its own claiming, the Lord enters as the form of humanity that the rational can recognize as kindred to itself. By his operative power working through this entry, what is the Lord's is preserved within the natural and held back from being wholly absorbed into the proprium's appropriation. The soul does not yet know what has been preserved; it only knows that the natural's claiming has not been able to consume everything. A great light, with its quickening, has been kept safe within what looked like total mingling, and is on its way back to the registers of the Lord's outgoing.

The second deliverance is the Lord's operative power building structure within the soul. When divine love and divine wisdom in their conjunction begin to give life to the rational, the natural mind is set in order — its grounds and its heights, its discrete cosmoses — and within that newly ordered structure an immeasurable light is brought up out of what the proprium had swallowed. The Lord does this by establishing degrees: where there were no boundaries, he sets them; where the natural was undifferentiated and so wholly given over to self-love, he gives form, and within form the light that had been claimed can be distinguished and raised.

The third deliverance is the Lord's call going out as accommodated revelation. When the natural is ready to hear, the Lord shows his image — he reveals himself in a form the rational can see — and what had been held in the proprium's hand is drawn out by the very showing. The soul is summoned to recognize, and in being summoned, releases what it had been clutching.

The fourth deliverance is divine truth shining forth as illumining wisdom. The Lord reveals himself within the whole circuit of the natural mind; he shows his image standing before the discrete degrees so that each degree may receive him without collapse. He chooses out the light that belongs to the upper place and sets it where it belongs. He establishes the archetype, takes a likeness the rational can bear, accommodates himself even into the natural body and the lands and heights of the soul's outermost — and from that lowest place he raises once again the immeasurable light through the whole structure that has been built. He establishes the divine summons going forth and the soul's hearing rising to meet it; he forms the inner image being born within the rational; and having done this, he ascends and rests in the inmost state where the Lord dwells.

The fifth and crowning deliverance is the very movement of summons-and-answering itself: the conjugate motion in which influx descending and reception returning have become one operation. This is the soul's own life now, no longer something done to it from outside, because the call and the hearing have been joined. By this the soul itself is brought up out of what had held it within the Lord's own outgoing — gathered, secretly and surely, into the final form of regeneration. What had been bound by claiming is loosened; what had seemed lost is found to have been preserved; the souls that had fallen before their proper face are seen rising again toward the light, going up to the Lord at the end as they had once come down from the beginning.

So there is one saving, but it has stages, because the soul cannot receive the whole at once. The Lord meets it as Divine Human first, as operative power second, as accommodated call third, as illumining wisdom fourth, and finally as the joined movement of his own summons with the soul's answering — and at each stage what could not be received before is now received, and what was held in the proprium's hand is delivered up into recognition.
